issues.problem: The new 'linear-time' assertion is an absolute wall-clock bound (<= 8 s for 64 KB through the Bash encoder) and fails under the coverage runner. CI's coverage job and the orchestrator's full run (run-coverage.sh --fail-under 100) execute it under BASH_ENV xtrace instrumentation, in the C.UTF-8 locale that tests/run-all-tests.sh:45-46 forces, and usually in parallel. The mandated scoped coverage run therefore exits 1 and the CI coverage gate is red by chance. The bound separates the old encoder only by a thin, load-dependent margin: old encoder 22 s, new encoder 6-10 s under coverage.
issues.evidence: Scoped coverage run (REVF-F1d-probe/cov.log, 32 test files, --jobs 2, load average 17-21 on 4 CPUs): 'FAIL: message via bash: 64 KB mixed string took 10s' -> 'TOTAL: 1474 passed, 1 failed', exit=1. An earlier interrupted run on the same host: 'is linear-time (66399 chars in 6s)'. The same test without coverage at load 9: 2 s. Encoder alone (scripts/enc-perf-loc.sh, same 64 KB string): LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 1045 ms, LC_ALL=C 401 ms. Mutation with the db79336 encoder (mut-m3): 'took 22s'.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop the absolute bound, or make it scale-relative: time 16 KB and 64 KB and require ratio < 8, or count replace iterations. If a bound is kept, make it generous (e.g. 60 s) or skip it when SB_COV_DIR is set. Also run the encoder in the C locale (issue 3), which roughly halves its time in the runner's locale. Assert full equality (json.loads(...) == text) rather than only the length.

issues.problem: printf -v 'ctl_ch[i]' assigns to an array element, which Bash added only in 4.1 (bash-4.1 NEWS: 'printf -v can now assign values to array indices'; bash-3.2 printf.def accepts only legal_identifier()). The review brief explicitly bans 'printf -v arrays' in hooks/. On macOS /bin/bash 3.2 each of the 28 assignments fails with 'not a valid identifier', ctl_ch stays empty, and no C0 control character other than \n \r \t is escaped. Any text containing one (an ANSI ESC, \x01, \x07, ...) then becomes an invalid JSON document from the last-resort encoder, contradicting the header's 'control characters always yield one valid document'. Each encoded string also writes 28 error lines to stderr. Today's callers on that path (no jq and no python3) pass static jq-missing text without control characters, so the current impact is the stderr noise. BASH_COMPAT=32 does not emulate this restriction, so the new BASH_COMPAT tests cannot catch it. db79336 used a scalar printf -v and was fine.
issues.evidence: No Bash 3.2 binary is available, so scripts/bash32-printf-shim.sh emulates 3.2's printf -v (rejects non-identifiers with status 2, as printf.def does). scripts/enc-b32.sh with BASH_COMPAT=32: 118ed0c + shim -> 'INVALID JSON: Invalid control character at: line 1 column 2', 'stderr lines: 28', the jq-missing message stays valid, and an ANSI-coloured reason is 'INVALID'. db79336 + shim -> 'roundtrip True', 0 stderr lines. 118ed0c without shim -> roundtrip True. grep shows this is the only printf -v array assignment in hooks/.
issues.suggested_fix: printf -v ch '%b' "\\0$oct"; ctl_ch[i]="$ch" (verified in REVF-F1d-probe/fixcand: shim run -> roundtrip True, 0 stderr lines). Optionally add a lint rule that rejects 'printf -v [^ ]*\[' in hooks/.

issues.problem: In a UTF-8 locale (the runner's default, and the usual user locale), Bash 5.2's "${rest%%"$bs"*}" returns 6 bytes of uninitialised heap memory (they change between runs and end in 0x55/0x56, a heap-pointer fragment) when the remaining string begins with a lone UTF-8 lead byte immediately followed by a backslash. The encoder then emits that garbage, drops the text that follows, and can produce invalid JSON. The bug is already present in db79336's replace loop (any text with '\\', a lone lead byte and then '\\'). Chunking adds a fresh trigger wherever a 256-character boundary falls just before such a byte. Reaching it needs no jq, no python3 and invalid UTF-8 next to a backslash, and today's callers pass static text, hence minor.
issues.evidence: scripts/enc-min.sh (LC_ALL=C.utf8): s=$'\xc3\\rest'; ${s%%"\\"*} -> '87 e0 7b 74 d6 55' (run 1), '2a e7 16 0e a7 55' (run 2); C locale -> 'c3'. scripts/enc-lead.sh: db79336 encoder on $'a\\\xc3\\b' -> '" a \\ \\ 361 326 $ 250 g U "' (garbage, trailing b lost); 118ed0c the same. Corpus of 2071 cases (scripts/enc-gen.py: multibyte, invalid and control bytes straddling 256-character boundaries, plus random soup), checked byte-for-byte with scripts/enc-check.py: LC_ALL=C 0 mismatches; C.utf8 4 mismatches (also under BASH_COMPAT=32/42), e.g. c01394 has 6 garbage bytes at offset 257, the first character of chunk 2. Plain substring concatenation of the same files is byte-exact (enc-substr.sh), so slicing is fine; the corruption is in %% pattern removal.
issues.suggested_fix: Add 'local LC_ALL=C' as the first line of _sb_hook_json_bash. The function only runs inside $(...), so nothing leaks, and the encoder is byte-oriented anyway. Add a regression case such as $'a\\\xc3\\b' under LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 to test-hook-output.sh.
